title: Steel Authority of India Ltd - 500113 - Announcement under Regulation 30 (LODR)-Earnings Call Transcript

summary.headline: SAIL Q4 FY26: PAT up 43% YoY on higher NSR and volumes; FY27 sales volume target 22 mn tons and capex guided to INR15,000 crore.
summary.overview: SAIL reported Q4 FY26 crude steel output of 4.9 mn tons (up 4% YoY), sales volume of 5.3 mn tons (up 4%) and turnover of INR30,541 crore (up 5%). PBT rose 48% and PAT 43% YoY in the quarter, and management said Q4 borrowings fell by INR3,200 crore. For FY26, record sales volume of 19.9 mn tons (up 11%) and a roughly 1 mn ton inventory reduction drove borrowings down about INR8,150 crore, and management said the FY26 balance sheet carries no audit qualifications for the first time in many years. Management said NSR rose about INR4,000/t from Q4 to April-May, while coking coal cost is also rising, with a stated impact of INR1,400-1,500/t in Q1 FY27.

financial_highlights.change: YoY, no rail price arrears in FY26 vs ~INR1,800 crore in FY25
management hopes to lower it in FY27

segments.name: Long products
segments.commentary: Q4 NSR INR53,400/t; April NSR INR57,600/t and mid-May about INR57,800/t. March long-product price increase was about INR1,500/t.

segments.name: Flat products
segments.commentary: Q4 NSR INR51,000/t; April INR56,700/t and mid-May about INR56,000/t. Flat price increase in March was about INR1,400/t. A safeguard duty on flat imports is in place.

segments.name: Bokaro Steel Plant
segments.commentary: EBITDA recovered sharply in H2 FY26 after FY25 breakdowns and a Hot Strip Mill repair that ran 2 months beyond plan. Better flat-product NSR and SMS fixes also helped, and management expects further improvement in FY27.

segments.name: Salem (stainless)
segments.commentary: Still loss-making. CR mill yield is 83-84% against a 90% target, and LPG has been replaced with PNG. Management plans to feed imported stainless slabs to idle CR and SR mill capacity.

segments.name: NSL / RINL volumes
segments.commentary: NSL total volume was 1.12 mn tons in FY26, with Q4 near 0.1 mn tons. Sales of RINL products began in February, at about 48,000-50,000 tons in Q4, and are guided at 0.6-0.7 mn tons in FY27.

guidance_outlook: FY27 sales volume target of 22 mn tons (about 22.5 mn tons including RINL products), up from 19.9 mn tons in FY26.
FY27 crude steel production target of 22.5 mn tons against stated capacity of 21 mn tons, to be reached through debottlenecking and operational efficiency.

Capex guidance: INR15,000 crore in FY27, INR18,000-19,000 crore in FY28, and INR20,000-25,000 crore per year after that, to be funded mainly from internal accruals with incremental long-term borrowings.
Coke rate target to fall by about INR20/kg in FY27 after the earlier reduction; management aims for a further drop in coke rate.

Employee strength is 49,752 as of 1 April 2026, with a further reduction of 3,400-3,500 expected in each of FY27 and FY28. A VRS targeting 500-1,000 exits is under way. Pay revision from 1 January 2027 is not yet in the guidance and will be provided for in Q4 FY27.

Q1 FY27 inventory: management aims for no build-up in Q1 and expects Q2 to be sluggish with inventory reduction in Q3 and Q4. Coking coal cost is up about INR2,000/t to about INR21,500/t, implying a cost impact of INR1,400-1,500/t on production cost.
capex_capacity: Crude steel capacity is 21 mn tons; FY26 output was 19.43 mn tons. FY27 target is 22.5 mn tons through debottlenecking and operating beyond rated capacity.

New capacity expansion projects at IISCO (about 4.5 mn tons, INR35,000-36,000 crore), Bhilai (about 3.5 mn tons, about INR30,000 crore, yet to be announced) and Bokaro (about 3 mn tons, about INR18,000 crore) are the three cleared expansions.

IISCO packages are tendered and groundwork is starting, with spending rising from FY28 and some spending in Q4 FY27. Bokaro and Bhilai spending is mainly expected from FY29; new capacity is expected from FY30-31.
Capex in FY27 covers debottlenecking, AMR (asset modernisation/replacement) and expansion projects.
Iron ore: FY26 production was 38 mn tons with a 56 mn ton target for FY27 and 80 mn tons as the longer-term ramp-up goal. The Chiria mine is a new lease, not a renewal.
demand_pricing: Indian steel consumption grew about 8% in FY26 while production grew 11%. India became a marginal net exporter, with exports of 6.5 mn tons and imports of 6.6 mn tons.
Q1 demand is expected to be muted, with destocking, then a pickup from Q3. Rupee depreciation and firmer international prices support landed cost and selling prices.

Cost pressure: the Middle East situation pushed up limestone/flux costs (CFR from about $23-24 to about $35/t), with an impact of only INR100-200/t on saleable steel. Fuel constraints were managed through PNG and LPG banks.
Rail freight prices: FY25 arrears were about INR1,800 crore; FY26 provisional rates are lower, and the FY25 rate finalisation could affect FY27. Management said the direction is unclear.
Flat safeguard duty and cheaper import blends are limiting import volumes.

qa_highlights.question: What are FY27 and FY28 volume guidance and capex plans?
qa_highlights.answer: FY27 sales target of 22 mn tons (vs 19.9 mn in FY26); FY27 capex INR15,000 crore against about INR9,100 crore in FY26; FY28 about INR18,000-19,000 crore; then INR20,000-25,000 crore per year.

qa_highlights.question: Realisations in Q4 and April-May, and cost outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Q4 blended NSR about INR52,000/t; April about INR57,000/t. Coking coal rose from INR18,200/t in Q4 to about INR21,000 in April and INR21,800 in May. Q1 consumption cost impact is smaller because of about 30 days of inventory.

qa_highlights.question: What is the capacity and the path to 22.5 mn tons?
qa_highlights.answer: Capacity is 21 mn tons. Growth to 22.5 mn tons comes from debottlenecking and efficiency gains, with new capacity only from FY30-31. Management said output could reach 23 mn tons later.

qa_highlights.question: How is the Q3 to Q4 EBITDA bridge explained?
qa_highlights.answer: Input prices were a INR272 crore headwind, offset by a INR429 crore gain from better raw-material usage (higher PCI, more oxygen, better iron ore use).

qa_highlights.question: Can 100%+ utilisation be sustained given the capacity figures?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said DPR capacity is not a hard limit for blast furnaces and SMS; productivity can exceed design, citing examples of 2.3 going to 3 and the operations of peers.

qa_highlights.question: How will the capex be funded and what is the leverage?
qa_highlights.answer: Management expects internal accruals to cover most of FY27 capex, with incremental long-term borrowings beyond that. Net debt to equity is 0.37 and is expected to fall further in FY27.

qa_highlights.question: Will working capital rise with the monsoon season?
qa_highlights.answer: Management aims for no inventory build in Q1 but said Q2 will be challenging, with inventory reduction planned for Q3 and Q4.

risks_watch: Wage revision from 1 January 2027: the impact is not yet in guidance and may be booked in Q4 FY27; past revisions were about 15%.
Coking coal and imported coal costs are rising, with the Q1 cost impact estimated at INR1,400-1,500/t against a NSR tailwind.
Q1 and Q2 demand softness and destocking; inventory build risk.
Rail freight price finalisation for FY25 could go either way in FY27.
Middle East supply disruption affecting fuel, flux and raw material routes (Strait of Hormuz).
Salem Steel Plant losses and BISL disinvestment status; the Chiria mining lease is still pending.
Achieving 22 mn tons on the 21 mn ton stated capacity and funding INR15,000 crore capex in FY27.
summary.management_tone: Confident and upbeat on FY26 profit growth, volume records and the clean audit position, with a clear FY27 target. Cautious on Q1-Q2 demand and on the outcome of the wage revision and rail price decisions, which management called unclear.
key_quotes: So far as expansions are concerned, actually, we've cleared for 3 plants.

Company has posted highest ever sales volume at 19.9 million tons, almost like 20 million tons, which margina lly -- I mean, it is close to 20 million tons with a growth of 11% as compared to the previous year.
after a pretty long time, many years and decades, you can say, that the balance sheet of '25 -'26 is totally clean from the qualifications.
But overall, in sellable steel, its impact will be hardly INR100 or INR200.
So you can say that the cost impact will be around INR1,400 to INR1,500 per ton.
